previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, and GERD was admitted for fever and confusion. He presented with a temperature of 102°F at home and was found to have elevated ammonia and mild leukocytosis. Initial evaluation included a spinal tap, imaging, and infectious workup, all of which were unremarkable except for a benign CSF and negative viral studies. He was treated with a dose of broad-spectrum antibiotics in the ED but showed no ongoing signs of infection. Lactulose was restarted for hepatic encephalopathy, and sirolimus was reduced to 2 mg daily to protect kidney function. The patient improved rapidly, remained afebrile, and was discharged home with instructions to continue lactulose, monitor mental status, and follow up with his primary and liver specialists.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ gentleman with CKD (baseline cr 1.5-1.8), 
cryptogenic cirrhosis s/p OLT in ___ (on Sirolimus + MMF) 
presented with myalgias and fevers to 101.
.
# Influenza-like-illness: Given patient's reported myalgias and 
fevers, his symptoms were concerning for influenza and he was 
started on empiric Tamiflu for 10 day course (extended treatment 
course given immunosuppression) since he was unable to tolerate 
the nasopharyngeal swab. CPK levels were normal.  Urine and 
blood culture were negative.  CXR did not show any pneumonia.  
His symptoms improved significantly in his hospital course. He 
remained afebrile for >48 hours before discharge and his 
myalgias had resolved. 
.
# Cryptogenic Cirrhosis s/p OLT now with Mild Liver Rejection: 
Patient was noted to have transaminitis which was initially 
thought to from viral illness.  CVM, hep b and hep c serologies 
were negative. However given persistent transaminitis there was 
concern for liver rejection. He had liver biospy with pathology 
showing mild cellular rejection. Patient's tacrolimus was 
increased to 3mg daily for goal level of ___. He was continued 
on MMF.  Additionally there was neutrophilic infiltration of 
biliary duct. Patient will have MRCP on ___ to 
evaluate for any signs of biliary pathology. Patient will have 
full sets of labs including rapamycin levels on ___ 
and follow up in the transplant clinic on ___.  Patient will 
need to be vaccinated against hep b.
.
# Type II diabetes:  Patient was also diagnosed with diabetes 
during this admission with HbA1c of 7.7%. He was encouraged to 
eat food with less carbohydrate intake. He will follow up with 
his PCP for further management.
.
# Chronic Kidney Disease: Creatinine post-transplant has wavered 
between 1.5-2.0. His Cr remained around baseline of 1.8.   
.
# GERD: Continued lansoprazole
.

PHYSICIANS:  ___

The procedure, risks, benefits and alternatives were discussed with the
patient and written informed consent was obtained.  A preprocedure timeout was
performed discussing the planned procedure, confirming the patient's identity
with three identifiers, and reviewing a checklist per ___ protocol.

Under ultrasound guidance, an entrance site was selected and the skin was
prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  1% lidocaine was instilled
for local anesthesia.

An 18-gauge biopsy needle was advanced into the right hepatic lobe under
ultrasound guidance via a right lateral intercostal approach and a single core
biopsy was obtained.

Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of 1.5mg versed
and 75 mcg fentanyl throughout the total intra-service time of 10 minutes
during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously monitored
by radiology nursing personnel.

The patient tolerated the procedure well with no immediate complication.
Estimated blood loss was minimal.  

Dr. ___ attending radiologist, was present throughout the entire
procedure.  Post-procedure instructions were written in the ___ medical
record.

IMPRESSION:
Ultrasound-guided 18 G non-targeted liver biopsy.  Pathology pending.

microbiology.comments: NO ANTIBODY TO B. BURGDORFERI DETECTED BY EIA.  Reference Range:  No antibody detected.  Negative results do not rule out B. burgdorferi infection.  Patients in early stages of infection or on antibiotic therapy may not produce  detectable levels of antibody.  Patients with clinical history and/or  symptoms suggestive of lyme disease should be retested in 2-3 weeks.

NEGATIVE FOR CMV IgM ANTIBODY BY EIA.  INTERPRETATION:  INFECTION AT UNDETERMINED TIME.  A positive IgG result generally indicates past exposure.  Infection with CMV once contracted remains latent and may reactivate when immunity is compromised.  If current infection is suspected, submit follow-up serum in 2-3 weeks.  Greatly elevated serum protein with IgG levels >2000 mg/dl may cause  interference with CMV IgM results.
